rules.specification: This page does not define plain language or prescribe vocabulary, sentence-length or readability thresholds.
rules.violation_condition: The text contains unnecessarily complex wording that obscures its meaning for the intended audience.
rules.why: G-4: the two plain-language instructions are one rule, not separate findings.

rules.violation_condition: A searchable content page has no headings.
rules.why: G-1: this is an independently checkable child instruction, rather than the section's general searchability goal.

covers.quote: Include keywords that users relate to the topic in headings and final paragraphs.

rules.quote: Embed keywords in the metadata and content.
rules.specification: Relevant keywords depend on the topic and users' search vocabulary. The page specifies metadata, headings and final paragraphs, but gives no keyword list, density target or requirement to repeat a keyword in every heading.
rules.violation_condition: Searchable content lacks relevant search keywords in its metadata or content, including the specified heading and final-paragraph locations.
when: For content intended to be found through search engines.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the general keyword instruction and its more specific placement wording to avoid overlapping missing-keyword findings.

examples.note: The form title precedes the reference number in the example search result.

parts.quote: Best search result: ‘Transfer your car to a new owner (Form 1066)’

rules.quote: If you include a reference number, place it after the form’s title so the algorithm can find the form.
rules.violation_condition: A form reference number appears before the form's title or without a preceding title.
when: When a form is identified using a reference number.
rules.why: G-2: including a reference number is the condition for the title-before-number check, not a separate requirement to include a number.

rules.quote: Level AAA requires a lower secondary education reading level, after removal of proper names and titles (year 7 or between 12 and 14 years old).
rules.specification: The stated benchmark is year 7 or ages 12–14. The page does not prescribe a readability formula or assessment method.
rules.violation_condition: Content required to meet Level AAA exceeds a lower-secondary reading level after proper names and titles are removed.
when: When WCAG Level AAA conformance is required.
Exclude proper names and titles from the reading-level assessment.
rules.why: G-2: Level AAA and the exclusion of names and titles limit one reading-level requirement.

rules.quote: Avoid (or explain) unusual words, phrases, idioms and so on.
rules.specification: What counts as unusual depends on the intended audience. The page does not specify the required form or location of an explanation.
rules.violation_condition: The text contains an unusual word, phrase or idiom without an explanation.
when: An unusual expression may remain if it is explained.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: avoidance and explanation are alternative ways to satisfy one check; explanation is an exception, not a separate rule.

rules.quote: Expand all acronyms on their first use.
rules.violation_condition: An acronym's first occurrence has no expansion.
when: Check the first occurrence of each acronym.
rules.why: The one-finding test separates missing acronym expansions from the preceding unusual-expression check.

rules.quote: To put the most important content at the top of the page, use the inverted pyramid.
rules.violation_condition: A page intended to present its most important content first places supporting or less important material ahead of that content.
when: For government content whose purpose calls for the most important information at the top.
rules.why: G-1 and G-2: retain this specific structural instruction and its stated purpose, rather than making the grouping heading another rule.

rules.quote: To lead people through a series of steps, use sequential structure.
rules.violation_condition: Content guiding users through a series of steps presents those steps out of the order needed to follow the process.
when: When the content leads people through a series of steps.
rules.why: G-1: sequential ordering is a distinct child check, not another version of importance ordering.

rules.quote: avoid words that sound similar to other words (homophones)
rules.violation_condition: Content intended to be found through voice search contains a homophone.
when: For content intended to be found through voice search.
rules.why: G-1: extract the specific voice-search wording check, not the descriptive heading.

rules.quote: create direct content that answers users’ questions.
rules.specification: The relevant user questions must be established before checking. The page does not define a quantitative test for a direct answer.
rules.violation_condition: Content intended to address a user's voice-search question provides no direct answer to that question.
when: For content intended to be found through voice search.
rules.why: G-1: direct answers are an independently checkable property of the content, separate from homophone avoidance.
